column1: # Platform seam registry — the source of truth for what crosses the platform boundary.
# Why this file exists
# A "seam" is a type bound differently in PlatformModule.android.kt and PlatformModule.jvm.kt.
# The repository has 25 of them. Ten have a JVM implementation that is an inert stub — the
# binding resolves, the caller calls it, and nothing happens. Nothing fails, because a
# no-op that is bound looks exactly like a no-op that works.
# Two Desktop bugs are live on origin/main today because of this:
#   - a reminder is written to Room and no alarm is ever armed (JvmReminderScheduler)
#   - every sync push evaporates on sign-in (NoopSyncWorkScheduler)
# The static unwired-surface detector cannot see any of it: `orphan-binding` hard-filters to
# CoreDiModule.kt, and it reports only bindings nothing injects. A port that is bound,
# injected and called — but inert — is outside its model.
# So the registry classifies every seam, and PlatformSeamGuardTest fails when:
#   - a seam's named implementation disappears from a platform module
#   - a seam marked `real` is actually a Noop/NoOp/Stub
#   - a seam marked `stub` carries no written reason
#   - a NEW typed binding appears in a platform module with no registry row  ← the load-bearing one
# That last rule is the point: seam 26 cannot be added silently.
# Format: pipe-separated, `#` starts a comment, blank lines ignored.
# Columns: port | kind | androidImpl | jvmImpl | verdict | reason
#   kind    seam  — platform-divergent; impl names are asserted
#           infra — infrastructure binding (paths, DataStore, scope); presence only
#   verdict real    — the JVM implementation genuinely works
#           stub    — the JVM implementation does nothing; reason is REQUIRED
#           exempt  — inert by deliberate, documented choice; reason is REQUIRED
#           infra   — not a behavioural seam
#   androidImpl / jvmImpl — a distinctive token that must appear in that platform's module.
#                            `-` when the platform has no binding (declared Android-only).
# Adding a binding? Add a row here first. The gate will remind you if you do not.
SyncPeriodicTrigger|seam|AndroidSyncPeriodicTrigger|DelayLoopSyncPeriodicTrigger|real|

GoogleSyncPeriodicTrigger|seam|AndroidGoogleSyncPeriodicTrigger|DelayLoopGoogleSyncPeriodicTrigger|real|Google sync runs on both platforms, so both bindings are real: WorkManager on Android, a delay loop on Desktop. Listed separately from SyncPeriodicTrigger because they are two schedulers for two features, and a row each is what stops one of them being dropped from a platform module unnoticed.
SyncWorkScheduler|seam|AndroidSyncWorkScheduler|NoopSyncWorkScheduler|stub|Every Desktop sign-in enqueues a push that evaporates. Replaced by the BackgroundWorkScheduler executor.

CalendarSyncWorkScheduler|seam|AndroidCalendarSyncWorkScheduler|NoopCalendarSyncWorkScheduler|stub|Calendar sync is Android-only by design; the Desktop settings UI is capability-gated so it cannot be mistaken for working.
ReminderScheduler|seam|AlarmManagerReminderScheduler|JvmReminderScheduler|stub|A Desktop reminder is written to Room and never fires. Replaced by the systemd --user scheduler.
CalendarSyncRepository|seam|CalendarSyncSettingsRepositoryImpl|NoopCalendarSyncRepositoryImpl|stub|Android-only feature. Its flowOf(false) is why the Desktop toggle used to stay visually ON.
CalendarProviderPort|seam|AndroidCalendarProvider|NoopCalendarProvider|stub|Android-only feature. Its Result.failure is the capability signal the Desktop UI now reads.
CalendarAppQueries|seam|AndroidCalendarAppQueries|JvmCalendarAppQueries|stub|Android-only feature; Desktop reports no installed calendar apps.
PomodoroTaskListProvider|seam|AndroidPomodoroTaskListProvider|JvmPomodoroTaskListProvider|stub|Returns an empty, never-updating list, which is indistinguishable from "no tasks selected".
PomodoroScheduler|seam|PomodoroAlarmScheduler|-|exempt|Android-only OS alarm. Desktop drives the pomodoro timer in-process instead.
NotificationPort|seam|AndroidNotificationPort|JvmNotificationPort|real|
BackupCodec|seam|AndroidBackupCodec|JvmBackupCodec|real|
SecureStoragePort|seam|AndroidSecureStorage|JvmSecureStorage|real|
FileSystem|seam|AndroidFileSystem|JvmFileSystem|real|
HostEnvironmentPort|seam|AndroidHostEnvironment|JvmHostEnvironment|real|
FileRevealer|seam|AndroidFileRevealer|JvmFileRevealer|real|
FileSourceFactory|seam|AndroidFileSourceFactory|JvmFileSourceFactory|real|
SharePort|seam|AndroidSharePort|JvmSharePort|real|
FileSharePort|seam|AndroidFileSharePort|JvmFileSharePort|real|
PomodoroTimer|seam|AndroidPomodoroTimer|JvmPomodoroTimer|real|
Haptic|seam|AndroidHaptic|createHaptic|exempt|Deliberate. Task detail composes haptics unconditionally, so a definition must exist on every platform or composition fails.

CrashReportingPort|seam|FileCrashReportingPort|JvmCrashReportingPort|exempt|Deliberate. Desktop logs through loggingBackgroundFailureHandler; a definition must exist or composition throws every frame.
# ── Infrastructure bindings: present on both platforms, not behavioural seams ──────────
AppDatabase|infra|-|-|infra|

UnitOfWork|infra|-|-|infra|RoomUnitOfWork on both platforms, not a seam: it is Room's own withWriteTransaction, and the Android and Desktop databases are the same type. Bound in both platform modules because both need the transaction, and registered here because a binding that appears in a platform module with no row is exactly what this file exists to make impossible. See ADR 2026-10-05-who-owns-a-row-and-the-patch-that-describes-it.
DataStore|infra|-|-|infra|
CoroutineScope|infra|-|-|infra|
String|infra|-|-|infra|
